title: Sequenced canary and signed image certification for intermittent-connectivity Private/VPC sites
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Some customers run Private/VPC deployments in environments with intermittent outbound connectivity and strict egress policies. Upgrades and operator-driven rollouts can fail or be unsafe if artifact provenance and image integrity cannot be validated, or if a canary that assumes steady control-plane connectivity is used. Goal: Define an operational contract and acceptance criteria for a sequenced canary rollout that works in limited-egress sites, combined with a lightweight signed-image certification (golden-image) workflow that allows local validation without full internet access. The solution must be auditable, actionable by on-call, and provide automated fallback to the last-known-good image without manual air-gapped media exchange.
scope_changes: Original scope was limited to canary traffic split rules. Expanded to include: 1) local image signature verification (cosign-compatible) with optional customer KMS integration; 2) bandwidth-aware artifact distribution strategy with resume/partial-fetch; 3) operator hooks for offline smoke tests and automatic rollback; 4) minimal telemetry that is privacy-respecting for degraded-network runs. Excluded: building a custom content distribution network or physical media shipping process.
acceptance_criteria: Canary orchestration: a two-phase canary that first validates operator-level health checks (node-level smoke tests) with no external egress and then opens a small percentage of traffic only when KV-cache and model indices are confirmed consistent.

Image attestation: images deployed to a Private/VPC site must carry a signed provenance statement (cosign or sigstore format) and be verifiable using a local trust bundle or customer KMS public key. Verification must succeed without outbound network calls. Failure prevents rollout.

Bandwidth-aware staging: artifact distribution supports chunked downloads with resume and local mirroring; rollout aborts gracefully if staging does not complete within a configurable timeout (default 2 hours).

Rollback: automated rollback to previously marked golden image completes within the configured SLA (default 15 minutes from detection of canary failure) and preserves tenant configs and KV cache where possible.

Operator smoke tests: a standardized operator test harness runs pre- and post-upgrade: container start, model-load (sanity token generation), RPC smoke test, and disk-mapped config validation; results are recorded in a local artifact store for audit.

Audit and telemetry: minimal local audit trail is written (checksums, signature verification result, canary test outcomes). If outbound telemetry is blocked, the system queues and exposes the same evidence via the Console when connectivity is restored.

Playbook: a documented runbook for manual intervention when image verification fails (steps to provide signed proof-of-source via Redwood support and optionally accept an operator-manual override with explicit risk acknowledgement).
decisions: Adopt cosign-compatible signatures for image attestation to maximize interoperability with customer tooling.
Trust bundle model: allow customers to provide a local trust bundle PEM or KMS public key; Redwood CA rotation optional but not required for offline validation.
Two-phase canary gating (operator smoke tests -> small traffic open) is the default for all Private deployments with 'limited-egress' label.
Implement chunked artifact fetch + local mirroring; do not implement physical media fallback in this sprint.
Telemetry default: store minimal audit locally and surface to Console when the site regains connectivity; do not send PII or model tokens in queued payloads.
open_questions: What is the minimum set of operator smoke tests customers expect across diverse hardware profiles (NVIDIA/AMD/CPU-only)?
For customers who refuse any outbound key exchange, do we allow a Redwood-signed emergency override? If so, what legal/ops guardrails are required?
How should we expose signature verification failures in the Console UI for non-operator users?
Is a 2-hour default staging timeout acceptable for low-bandwidth sites, or should we offer a longer default and a strict SLA for enterprise customers?

notes: Implementation should minimize operational surface for on-prem operators. Engineering to add a debug-only verbose mode that writes full verification artifacts to a local index file; by default only summary evidence is retained. We will coordinate with Solutions to add a consent workflow for customers to allow temporary outbound verification during pilot runs.
